text:
Alex: Quick ask — can we get a zone-by-zone econ snapshot for inference (A100/80GB and H100 pools) across US-EAST, US-WEST, EU-WEST, and AP-SOUTHEAST? Need: effective $/GPU-hour (including commit discounts), egress per TB, and a short note about latency/regional constraints. Target: decision for Q3 reserve mix.

Maria: Do you want spot included or only reserved/committed? Also include preemptions for spot if possible.

Alex: Include both. For spot show effective cost assuming 20% availability loss (timeout/evict). For reserved show 1yr vs 3yr blended. Keep it short — one slide's worth.

Tyler: I'll pull the billing rollups. Quick heads-up: our EU-WEST H100 pricing uses a custom commitment rate after last month's vendor rebate, so watch list pricing vs invoice.

Jia: Started a quick run. Past-30d on-host GPU-hrs + committed discounts from billing API. Early numbers (very rough):
```
Region     | GPU    | Spot $/hr | Reserved(1yr) $/hr | Egress $/TB
US-EAST    | A100   | 0.90      | 1.45               | 40
US-WEST    | A100   | 0.95      | 1.50               | 35
EU-WEST    | A100   | 1.10      | 1.60               | 55
AP-SOUTHEAST| A100  | 1.20      | 1.75               | 80
US-EAST    | H100   | 1.60      | 2.40               | 40
EU-WEST    | H100   | 1.90      | 2.70               | 55
```
Numbers include blended commit discounts where a regional reserved commit exists. Still need to add network egress cross-region multipliers and SLO latency notes.

Sam: Egress numbers look high for APAC — that's consistent with partner routing. Also note that our private customers require regional placement (no cross-region egress allowed) which tilts the decision to reserving more in AP-SOUTHEAST for dedicated capacity.

Maria: Can we run the same with an added column for "fallback cost" — i.e., if region saturated, how much extra we pay to route to nearest region (including ingress+egress + cold-start penalty)?

Tyler: I can approximate fallback using last-mile egress + cross-region bandwidth. SQL I used (BigQuery):
```sql
SELECT region, gpu_type, SUM(gpu_hours) AS hours, SUM(cost) AS raw_cost,
  SUM(commit_discount) AS commit_disc
FROM `redwood-billing.gpu_usage.usage_v2`
WHERE invoice_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY region, gpu_type
```
Plugging commit_disc into effective $/hr.

Jia: Added fallback column — rough delta to nearest region: US-WEST -> US-EAST +0.25 $/hr, EU-WEST -> US-EAST +0.40 $/hr, AP-SOUTHEAST -> closest (US-WEST) +0.55 $/hr. If you include egress for cross-region, APAC becomes > +0.85 $/hr.

Alex: Good. Any anomalies in the invoices? Tyler mentioned rebates.

Tyler: Yup — vendor rebate in EU-WEST masked as a credit in September invoice. Net effective reserved cost for EU-WEST H100 dropped ~18% but it's one-time; don't assume recurring.

billing-bot: Automated note: invoice anomalies detected for project 'infra-prod' in EU-WEST on 2026-01-02: credit 0.17 * monthly_commit_charge. See /billing/invoices/2026-01-EUW for details.

Sam: Ops constraints: AP-SOUTHEAST has GPU procurement latency (image bake + kernel tuning) of ~12h vs 3h in US regions. That increases cold-start penalty for on-demand scaleouts. For dedicated/reserved pools we amortize that so it's less of an issue.

Maria: For decisioning we should present 3 scenarios: conservative (more reserved in-region), aggressive (push spot+fallback), and hybrid (reserve base + spot burst). Can we get numerical % cost change vs current baseline?

Jia: I'll produce a 1-pager with: cost table (per-region, per-gpu), fallback delta, egress buckets, and operational notes (procurement latency, regulatory constraints). ETA EOD tomorrow.

Alex: Perfect. Assigning: Jia for the one-pager, Tyler for billing validation (validate rebates/credits), Sam for ops constraints writeup. Maria to synthesize Q3 reserve mix recommendation.

Tyler: Noted. I'll also add a quick SQL to flag monthly non-recurring credits so Maria's recommendation excludes one-offs.

Alex: Thanks team — this will feed the Budget + Platform planning sync on Friday. :thumbsup:

Sam: Ping me when the one-pager's done, I'll run a quick simulation for customer-dedicated scenarios.

Maria: Adding a checklist to the doc:
- verify invoice credits (Tyler)
- compute fallback cost matrix (Jia)
- simulate dedicated customer constraints (Sam)
- produce recommendation and commit asks (Maria)

billing-bot: Scheduled export: /billing/exports/region-econ-2103456789.csv will be ready in 2 hours.
